item.description:
Hold a key, speak, release. The text lands at your cursor. Nothing leaves the machine.
This one is mostly about time. Text reaches the cursor sooner, and everything that happens after it, from the history entry to the panel to the extensions that asked for your transcript, no longer waits for a step it never needed. An extension can also put a sign over your screens now, and offer you text to copy.
## Text arrives sooner
With cleanup on, utt tidies each paragraph on the on-device model before it pastes. It used to do them one after another. It now does them all at once, and the model gets through overlapping requests faster than the same requests in turn. The text is exactly what it was. Only when it arrives has changed.
An 11-second dictation now reaches the cursor in about 1.8 s instead of 2.0 s, and a 30-second one in 3.4 s instead of 3.8 s.
## Nothing waits for the clipboard any more
After pasting, utt puts back whatever was on your clipboard. To be sure the app you were in had read the text first, it waited half a second, and the history entry, the panel and every extension waited with it. The clipboard is still put back after the same half second, but nothing else waits for it.
Extensions that receive your transcripts hear about it about 0.7 s sooner.
## Extensions are answered as soon as they speak
utt used to check an extension's folder on a timer: every 300 ms for audio it had been sent, every 50 ms for a filter's answer. It now watches those folders and reacts the moment a file lands, and the timer is kept only as a safety net. A clip an extension hands utt starts transcribing about 90 ms sooner, and a filter that answers at once now costs a millisecond instead of fifty.
Audio that arrives without a key press, from an extension or over the API, now also gets the cleanup model ready while it is being transcribed, as a dictation already did. Together these take an 11-second extension clip from 2.3 s to 1.9 s.
## An extension can put a sign over your screens
An extension can name a local address in its manifest, and utt will ask it every two seconds whether there is something to show. If there is, utt draws it across every screen, just below the Dock, without taking the mouse or the keyboard. Any touch of either takes it down at once: your own input always comes first.
Only an address on this Mac is accepted. Anything else is ignored, and the extension's log says why.
## An extension can offer text to copy
An extension can list snippets in its manifest. Its page shows each one in full, selectable, with a **Copy** button that utt serves itself, so it works even when the extension is not running. Invisible characters are stripped, so what you see is what you paste.
## Usage counts, if you want them
**General → Send anonymous usage counts** is off, and stays off unless you switch it on. When it is on, utt reports that it launched and that a transcription finished, whether you dictated it or an extension or the API handed it in: the engine, the model, how many seconds it ran, and whether the text arrived. It never sends the words, never the audio, and never which app received them. There is no field for any of that to travel in.
## Updating
Nothing you have set up needs redoing.
